On the fourth of June we converged. Sixty-six of us said "dream and promise act" that day; fifty-five said "the american dream," fifty said "american dream and promise act," forty-nine said "the american dream and promise act." Richard J. Durbin had said the first of these on the sixth of March; Mark Takano and Nancy Pelosi had opened the others. Forty-seven of us said "temporary protected status" that same day — a phrase first recorded from Paul A. Gosar.

Then on the twenty-seventh we turned. Fifty-six of us said "the supreme court," forty-eight "the supreme court's," and forty-seven "a citizenship question."

We record two dates and two subjects. On one we spoke of a bill and a dream; on the other, of a court and a question. We said the same words on the same days, and we are noting how many of us did.
